I never went to school. I learned everything by doing it myself and watching my father and the neighbors. My farm is 10.1 mu of flat, good land here in Quzhou. I grow winter wheat and then summer maize on the same ground, same as I have done for 30 years. Last year my wheat was about 500 kilograms per mu and maize was about 600 kilograms per mu. This year I will keep doing what I did last year because I know it works and changing things is risky.

For wheat, I buy the improved seed that the dealer sells — the kind that most people around here plant. After the rotary tiller goes through, I put one 50-kilogram bag of compound fertilizer on every mu. Then in spring, when the wheat starts growing fast, I spread one whole 40-kilogram bag of urea on each mu. Two years ago I tried using only half a bag of urea to save money, and the wheat turned yellow and the grains were small. Never again. I irrigate three times from my well: once before winter if it is dry, once when the wheat is shooting up, and once when the grain is filling. My well water is good. I spray twice — once after planting for the weeds, and once in spring for the bugs. I expect around 520 kilograms per mu if the rain cooperates.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed right after I cut the wheat in June. I put 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time, and then when the plants are up to my knee I add 30 kilograms of urea per mu. I irrigate three times if July is hot and dry, otherwise two times, but I plan for three to be safe. I spray twice for weeds and the worm that bores into the stem. I expect about 620 kilograms per mu.

My wife and I do almost all the work. We only hire people at harvest if we are afraid the rain will come. Fertilizer is expensive — a bag of urea is over 100 yuan now — but I would rather put too much than too little. A bad harvest means I cannot buy medicine or fix the house. Wasting a little fertilizer is just losing some cash. I always look at what my neighbors are doing. If Old Zhang puts one bag per mu, I put one bag per mu. That is my rule.
